definition: Quality of care is how well health services meet justified clinical aims and the needs of the people receiving them.
explanation: A full judgment can consider whether care is safe, effective, centered on the patient, timely, efficient, and equitable. The relevant evidence and trade-offs depend on the service and population.
A favorable outcome alone does not settle whether the care was good. The way care was delivered, foreseeable risks, and the patient’s circumstances also matter.
